record.question:
A hospital runs a three-tier web application with unpredictable demand. Users must retain their sessions when an application instance is replaced. Most database traffic consists of read-only reports that can tolerate brief replication lag, and peak report traffic exceeds the capacity of one database instance. The application must also recover automatically from a database Availability Zone failure.

Which architecture meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Auto Scaling groups for web and application instances, keep sessions on each instance, and deploy an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance without read replicas.
Use Auto Scaling groups for web and application instances, keep sessions on each instance, and use an RDS Single-AZ primary with read replicas.

Use stateless web and application instances in Auto Scaling groups with CloudWatch-based scaling policies. Store shared sessions in a resilient ElastiCache deployment. Use an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance and direct reporting queries to read replicas.

Use stateless web and application instances in Auto Scaling groups with CloudWatch-based scaling policies. Store shared sessions in a resilient ElastiCache deployment. Direct all queries to an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance without read replicas.

explanation.text:
<<3>> addresses three separate scaling and availability concerns. External session storage lets requests move between application instances. RDS read replicas offload lag-tolerant reads, while a Multi-AZ DB instance provides a synchronous standby for automatic failover. Size and configure the session store for its own availability and recovery needs.

<<1>> retains instance-local sessions and does not offload reports. <<2>> still loses local sessions when instances are replaced and lacks the requested Multi-AZ primary/standby failover design. <<4>> solves session placement and database failover but sends the excessive read workload to the primary.

A standby in an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment does not serve reads. This differs from an RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster, whose reader instances can serve queries. Monitoring alone also does not scale instances; configure scaling policies and route read traffic explicitly.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-target-tracking.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/framework/rel_mitigate_interaction_failure_stateless.html

diagram_alt: The session store, asynchronous read replicas and synchronous standby solve different problems.

sources.supports: Multi-AZ DB instance synchronous standby supports failover but not read traffic.
Asynchronous read replicas offload read-only queries.
Target tracking uses CloudWatch metrics to adjust Auto Scaling capacity.
Offloading sessions to ElastiCache allows stateless compute replacement and horizontal scaling.

editorial_notes: Made session survival and read capacity explicit so the answer is uniquely justified.
Qualified the standby limitation to Multi-AZ DB instance deployments.
